column3: NASB follows the critical text (“from Jesus Christ,” without “Lord”).
“Rejoiced exceedingly” is rendered “was very glad”; NASB supplies “to do.”
NASB follows the critical text (“have gone out”); “confessing” is rendered “acknowledge,” and NASB adds “as.”
NASB follows the critical text (“you … lose,” “you may receive”); “worked for” is rendered “accomplished.”
NASB follows the critical text (“goes too far”; “the teaching,” without “of Christ” the second time).
“Tell him to rejoice” is rendered “give him a greeting.”
“Telling him to rejoice” is rendered “gives him a greeting.”
NASB follows the critical text (“come”), but it reads “your joy” with the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “our joy.” “Mouth to mouth” is rendered “face to face.”
NASB follows the critical text, without “Amen”; “elect” is rendered “chosen.”
